Core building blocks

The patterns next.dj adds, each shown in real project source.

File router

Pages are files

Add a directory with a page.py under pages/ and it answers a URL. Groups in parentheses organise the tree without touching the URL, and an intercepting route opens a page over the current one.

  • {{ check() }} Directories become URL segments, no urls.py
  • {{ check() }} [int:id] captures a typed path parameter
  • {{ check() }} (app)/ shares a layout or an access rule and adds no segment
  • {{ check() }} (.) opens a page as a modal while its URL stays honest
{{ mockbar("photos/pages/") }} 
(auth)/
  layout.djx                # wraps every page below
  login/page.py             /login/
(app)/
  page.py                   # login_required(inherit=True)
  photos/
    page.py                 /photos/
    [int:id]/page.py        /photos/<int:id>/
    (.)[int:id]/page.py     # modal over /photos/<int:id>/
Components

Composable components

Call components by name, pass props, and fill named slots with child markup.

  • {{ check() }} One tag, {% raw %}{% component %}{% endraw %}, for every component
  • {{ check() }} Props are explicit, slots fill block content
  • {{ check() }} CSS and JS beside the component ship only when it renders
{{ mockbar("pages/template.djx") }} 
{% raw %}{% #component{% endraw %} "card" title="Welcome" %}
  {% raw %}{% #slot{% endraw %} "content" %}
    <p>Latest update.</p>
  {% raw %}{% /slot %}{% endraw %}
{% raw %}{% /component %}{% endraw %}
Forms

Forms that register themselves

Subclass next.forms.ModelForm with no URL to define. The framework attaches the POST endpoint, CSRF, and a re-render pipeline, and a failed submission returns the page with the user's input intact.

  • {{ check() }} No urls.py entry and no view to write
  • {{ check() }} On a failed submit the user keeps what they typed
  • {{ check() }} instance_from_url loads the edit row from the URL
  • {{ check() }} FormWizard spans steps without session juggling
{{ mockbar("notes/pages/note/[slug]/page.py") }} 
import next.forms

class NoteForm(next.forms.ModelForm):
    class Meta:
        model = Note
        fields = ["title", "body"]
        instance_from_url = "slug"
Partial rendering

Update a slice, not the page

Wrap a region in {% raw %}{% zone %}{% endraw %} and point a form, filter, or link at it. The server re-renders only that slice and ships the DOM patches the client applies. No endpoint, no JavaScript, and a full page load as the fallback.

  • {{ check() }} data-next-trigger auto-submits, morph keeps focus and caret
  • {{ check() }} The server authors every patch, selectors never cross the wire
  • {{ check() }} Modals and toasts ride the same protocol
  • {{ check() }} Every interaction degrades to a plain request without JS
{{ mockbar("wiki/pages/search/template.djx") }} 
{% raw %}<form method="get"
      data-next-target="search-results"
      data-next-trigger="input" data-next-debounce="300">
  <input name="q" value={{ query }}>
</form>

{% zone "search-results" %}
  {% for hit in results %}
    <a href={{ hit.url }}>{{ hit.title }}</a>
  {% endfor %}
{% endzone %}{% endraw %}
Realtime

Every open tab stays current

A mutation publishes a zone refresh to a topic. Each page subscribed to it fetches that zone again through its own guarded request, so no tab ever receives HTML rendered for someone else.

  • {{ check() }} publish fires once the transaction commits
  • {{ check() }} WebSocket where the process mounts it, SSE everywhere else
  • {{ check() }} RedisBroker fans out across workers and hosts
  • {{ check() }} Plain ASGI, no Django Channels and no channel layer
{{ mockbar("polls/pages/polls/[int:id]/page.py") }} 
import next.forms
from next.partial import Patches
from next.realtime import publish

class VoteForm(next.forms.Form):
    choice = next.forms.ModelChoiceField(queryset=Choice.objects.all())

    def on_valid(self, request: HttpRequest) -> HttpResponse:
        choice = self.cleaned_data["choice"]
        Choice.objects.filter(pk=choice.pk).update(votes=F("votes") + 1)
        publish(
            f"poll:{choice.poll_id}",
            Patches(request).refresh(zone="poll-results"),
        )
        return redirect_to_origin(request)
Access

Access rules live in the tree

A page.py declares who may open its page, and with inherit=True every page below it. The page's actions and zone requests answer to the same rule.

  • {{ check() }} login_required, permission_required, and public in Django's own terms
  • {{ check() }} DObject[Book] checks the permission on the row the URL names
  • {{ check() }} add_perm backs user.has_perm with a plain predicate
  • {{ check() }} manage.py permissions prints the rule of every page
{{ mockbar("library/pages/library/book/[int:book]/page.py") }} 
from library.models import Book

from next import page
from next.deps import DObject

page.login_required(inherit=True)
page.permission_required("library.change_book", obj=DObject[Book])
SEO

Metadata that follows the tree

A page.py names its title and description, and the page tree layers them from the root down. {% raw %}{% metadata %}{% endraw %} renders the head, and a sitemap.py beside the pages publishes /sitemap.xml.

  • {{ check() }} A static metadata dict reaches every page below it
  • {{ check() }} @page.metadata reads the row the page already loaded
  • {{ check() }} Canonical links and Open Graph tags build on the site origin
  • {{ check() }} manage.py showmetadata names the source of every key
{{ mockbar("notes/pages/notes/[int:note_id]/page.py") }} 
from next import context, page
from next.pages import MetadataDict
from next.urls import DUrl

@context("note")
def note(note_id: DUrl[int]) -> Note:
    return get_object_or_404(Note, pk=note_id)

@page.metadata
def note_metadata(note: Note) -> MetadataDict:
    return {"title": note.title, "og": {"type": "article"}}
Dependency injection

Inject by signature

Declare what a page or action needs as typed parameters. The resolver matches each one to a provider and supplies it.

  • {{ check() }} Parameters resolve by name, type, and marker
  • {{ check() }} @resolver.dependency publishes a named value
  • {{ check() }} Depends("name") pulls it into any signature
{{ mockbar("pages/notes/[int:note_id]/page.py") }} 
from django.http import HttpRequest
from next.deps import Depends
from next.pages import context
from next.urls import DUrl

@context("note")
def note(
    request: HttpRequest,
    note_id: DUrl[int],
    repo: NoteRepo = Depends("note_repo"),
) -> Note:
    return repo.for_user(request.user).get(pk=note_id)

next.dj ships more than these blocks. Co-located static assets, root layouts, a test client that knows the router, signals, and the full reference live in the documentation.
